Catalogue of the Ashreach Sale
A Marsh-Holding Offered Under Seal, with Conditions of Contest
> To all creditors, claimants, captains, and persons of sound enough judgment to bid: > Let it be
known that Ashreach is presented for auction—not as a jewel, nor as a refuge, but as a defended holding in
a country where water remembers every footprint. > —From the hand of the appointed catalogue-keeper
The Holding Entire
Ashreach lies in The Weeping Marshes and is currently contested. Its garrison numbers 2598, making
it a defended but unsettled holding rather than a core stronghold.
The prudent bidder will read those words twice.
The walls—where wall may be distinguished from bank, bank from ruin, and ruin from drowned
foundation—are offered with the settlement. So too the perpetual burden of watchfulness. Ashreach
presents the bleak, marsh-bound aspect of a settlement caught between ash and water. Its atmosphere is
tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened.
No claim is made here that the holding is peaceful. No claim is made that it is safe. The catalogue merely
records that it stands, and that standing in The Weeping Marshes is itself a form of defiance.
Lot A — The Ashen Ground
An extent of blackened earth and wet margin, suitable to those who prefer their inheritance difficult to
reach and more difficult to keep. Mist is included without surcharge. The mud is deep, the air close, and
the horizon frequently unwilling to appear.
The lot is offered as part of Ashreach and may not be separated from its unsettled condition.
Lot B — The Garrison
The garrison numbers 2598.
Arms, discipline, loyalties, and appetites are not warranted by this catalogue. The catalogue-keeper
records only the number and leaves the buyer to discover what manner of defense is purchased with it.
A defended holding is not thereby a secure holding. Any clerk who says otherwise has never slept beneath
a roof while the marsh whispered against the door.
Lot C — The Claim
Ashreach is offered amid the broader contention over the ruins by The Ashen Vanguard, House
Morvain, the Silent Choir, the Iron-Ring Cartel, and the Bleeding Crown.

Their interest, if interest it be, is not represented as consent, surrender, or absence. The holding remains
currently contested, and bidders are advised that ink has less weight than steel when both are set upon the
same boundary.
Final Notice
Ashreach is not sold as a core stronghold. It is sold as a defended but unsettled holding: bleak,
marsh-bound, caught between ash and water, tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened.
Bids shall be spoken plainly.
The marsh has little patience for mumbling.

Catalogue of Lantern and Ledger — Draven Ashgrove
& Halvard Sablewood
Issued beneath the soot-black seal of the auction hall, for those who prize a name more highly than a face.
Draven Ashgrove
Description: A minor character of the Ashen Era, born in 382 AS. Draven Ashgrove serves as a
Lantern-Warden.
Nature of the Offering: The purchaser is invited to bid upon the written account of his office, the
authority implied by his title, and the lingering worth of a name carried beneath a hooded lamp. No blade,
cloak, lantern, seal, or other personal article is entered here. Let no grasping hand claim otherwise when
the hammer falls.
Appearance: No physical features are recorded. His visual identity is associated with the office of a
Lantern-Warden. Thus the imagination supplies what the record withholds: the lamp before the face, the
warding sign, the figure standing where the dark is deepest. Such impressions are not evidence, but
auctions have never prospered on evidence alone.
Demeanor: No temperament is recorded. Buyers are cautioned against purchasing their own
assumptions under Draven Ashgrove’s name.
Condition: The account is intact insofar as the record is intact. Its silences are genuine and should not be
polished away. The hall accepts no complaint that the subject fails to resemble a portrait that was never
made.
Halvard Sablewood
Description: A minor figure of the Ashen Era, born in 408 AS. Halvard Sablewood serves as a scribe.
Nature of the Offering: Offered here is the scribe’s standing as a keeper of written matter: the authority
suggested by a hand that copies, marks, preserves, and perhaps outlasts the mouths of the living. No
manuscript, quill, desk, robe, or private document is included. The catalogue sells the account, not the
furniture imagined around it.
Appearance: No canonical physical details are recorded. His visual identity is associated with the
work of a scribe. Buyers may picture ink-stained fingers, bent shoulders, or a patient eye, but the
catalogue will not swear to any of these. A profitable fiction remains a fiction.
Demeanor: His canonical temperament is unrecorded. The hall therefore offers no promise of
meekness, severity, diligence, deceit, or any other quality a bidder might wish to attach to Halvard
Sablewood.
Condition: Unadorned, incomplete, and resistant to embellishment. The record bears what it bears. The
rest is silence, and silence has fetched a handsome price in less honest rooms.
Bids are accepted in names, oaths, or other tender deemed acceptable by the auctioneer. All claims are
final once spoken aloud.

# **The Greyfell Catalogue of Abandoned Stone**
### *An Auction of Salvage, Relics, and Unclaimed Remnants from Greyfell Citadel*

> **To all creditors, collectors, oath-breakers, and persons of sufficient nerve:**  
> The following catalogue concerns the remains of Greyfell Citadel, founded in **62 AS** within the **Shattered Vale**. The Citadel is abandoned and lies outside the realm’s core holdings. No warranty is offered regarding sanctity, safety, ownership, or the continued good sense of any purchaser.

Greyfell is not presented as a handsome ruin. Its visual identity is one of grey stone and grey-hued collapse, rising from the Shattered Vale like a tooth left in a dead jaw. Whatever banners once hung there have been taken by weather or hand. Whatever garrison once watched the approaches has gone. The place retains the demeanor of an old desolation, its former stronghold status reduced to abandonment.

The auctioneer records that each offering has been removed from the Citadel or its immediate fallen works. Buyers shall judge the truth of this claim according to their own consciences.

---

## **Catalogue of Offerings**

### **The Gatehouse Ironwork**
Bent hinges, corroded fastenings, and a length of darkened bar. Useful to those who desire the appearance of old authority without the burden of maintaining a gate.

### **The Grey Chapel Stone**
A dressed block bearing shallow marks too worn for confident reading. It has been cleaned only of loose dirt. The purchaser is advised not to ask what prayers were once spoken over it.

### **The Watch-Seat**
A broken stone chair from an upper passage, with one arm intact. It is uncomfortable, cold, and entirely suited to the ruling temperament.

### **The Ashen Archive Board**
A warped board with traces of pegs and cord. No papers accompany it. Its former purpose is unknown, which makes it desirable to those who prefer mystery to evidence.

### **The Cistern Chain**
A length of iron chain, heavily scaled, offered as found. Whether it served water, prisoners, or some uglier need cannot be established.

### **The Valeward Shards**
Fragments of grey masonry gathered from a collapsed outer wall. They are suitable for memorials, thresholds, grave-markers, or the construction of another place destined to be abandoned.

### **The Unclaimed Standard-Rod**
A splintered staff with no surviving device. The wood is darkened, the metal collar pitted. It bears no readable allegiance.

### **The Citadel Dust**
Sealed in a plain vessel. The catalogue clerk insists it is masonry dust. The clerk has not opened the vessel.

---

All sales are final. No purchaser may claim that Greyfell Citadel was misrepresented: it is a ruin of grey stone in the Shattered Vale, founded in **62 AS**, abandoned, and outside the realm’s core holdings. Its silence is included without additional charge.

Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
Issued for the consideration of bidders who prize dangerous knowledge above comfort. Provenance is sworn only where plainly stated; all other descriptions remain the house’s judgment.
HALVARD SABLEWOOD — The Scribe’s Parcel
A modest parcel of copied leaves, ruled scraps, and sealed blanks, offered as an evocation of Halvard Sablewood, a minor figure of the Ashen Era. The leaves bear no boast of authorship. Their value lies in the habits they suggest: ordered margins, patient corrections, and the cold discipline of a hand trained to preserve what stronger folk would burn.
Halvard Sablewood was born in 408 AS. He serves as a scribe. No canonical physical details are recorded for him; his visual identity is associated with the work of a scribe. His canonical temperament is unrecorded.
The house warns bidders against purchasing a face where none has been given, or a personality where the record is silent. What is offered is the shadow of a vocation: ink, sequence, silence, and the keeping of other people’s words.
MORWENNA ASHGROVE — Admiral’s Intelligence Packet
A sealed packet of naval-form memoranda, offered under the name and station of Morwenna Ashgrove. The contents are not opened before bidding. Such restraint is prudent when the subject is a major Fleet Admiral whose authority is disciplined on the surface and darkened beneath it.
Morwenna Ashgrove was born in 288 AS. She is a major Fleet Admiral. Morwenna secretly sells intelligence to the Iron-Ring Cartel.
No canonical physical features are established. Her visual identity is defined by the commanding station of Fleet Admiral. Her demeanor projects disciplined authority shadowed by covert dealings.
The packet is therefore sold not as a portrait, but as a danger: command rendered into paper, loyalty folded into trade, and silence made profitable. Bidders are advised that secrecy is not the same as safety.
HOLLOWVALE — Garrisoned Vale Prospectus
A charcoal prospectus of Hollowvale, its walls and approaches rendered beneath the black sweep of the Blood-Moor. The drawing presents a defended vale surrounded by ominous country, with watchfulness built into every ridge and gate.
Hollowvale was founded in 286 AS in the Blood-Moor. It is garrisoned by 7,594 troops and remains outside the realm’s core holdings.
Its visual identity is that of a defended vale encircled by the Blood-Moor’s threatening landscape. Its demeanor is guarded vigilance, sustained by a substantial garrison.
The prospectus contains no promise of welcome. It offers instead the hard comfort of walls, sentries, and distance from the realm’s core holdings. Those who bid should remember: a place may stand apart without standing free.
The auction house accepts no blame for knowledge acquired, secrets exposed, or valleys that continue to watch after the lamps are extinguished.

Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
Lot: Isolde Mournvale
Offered under the Ashen Era’s customary rule that a name may be weighed even when no treasure attends it, this entry concerns Isolde Mournvale, a minor figure of the Ashen Era.
She was born in 341 AS.
The surviving record gives her service plainly: Isolde Mournvale serves as a falconer. Beyond this office, the catalogue must proceed with an empty hand. No authenticated portrait, signet, garment, weapon, feather, hood, glove, or other possession is attached to her entry here. Buyers who seek painted eyes, noble blood, battlefield distinction, or a tale sharpened by repetition are warned that none may be supplied from the record.
Description
No canonical physical details are recorded for Isolde Mournvale.
Her visual identity is therefore not fixed by face, height, scars, coloring, age, or dress. It is associated instead with the work of a falconer: the discipline of handling a hunting bird, the patience required before release, and the silent attention given to a creature that may depart without farewell. These are the signs by which artists, chroniclers, and household rememberers may imagine her office, but they must not be mistaken for recorded features of her person.
Temperament
Isolde Mournvale’s canonical temperament is unrecorded.
The catalogue offers no judgment concerning her courage, cruelty, loyalty, wit, piety, obedience, or temper. Any seller who praises her gentleness, condemns her severity, or claims that she loved or feared anything speaks beyond the warrant of this entry. Such claims may be recited in taverns, painted upon banners, or whispered beside a mews, but they do not belong to the authenticated description.
Condition of Record
The name is legible. The birth year is given. The occupation is given. The remainder is silence.
This silence is not damage to be repaired by ornament. It is the present condition of the record concerning Isolde Mournvale. No estimate is placed upon her renown, for the catalogue establishes none. No provenance is claimed beyond the statement that she is a minor figure of the Ashen Era. No likeness is guaranteed, and no demeanor may be inferred as fact.
Purchaser’s Notice
The successful claimant receives neither a body nor a legend, but an entry bounded by what can be said. Let the buyer remember: where the record ends, invention begins.

Catalogue of Ashen Relics and Persons of Note
For the Consideration of Bidders Beneath a Sound Roof
Entry: Lucan Hollowmere
Name: Lucan Hollowmere Calling: Herbalist Birth: 296 AS
Lucan Hollowmere is entered here as a minor figure of the Ashen Era, though the hand that prepared this
catalogue admits that “minor” is a judgment made by the living and not always trusted by the dead.
He serves as an Herbalist. Beyond that service, the records grow thin. No canonical physical details are
recorded for Lucan Hollowmere. His visual identity is associated with the work of an herbalist: gathered
leaves, bitter roots, stained vessels, and the patient sorting of what heals from what merely delays the
grave.
His demeanor is unrecorded. Buyers are therefore cautioned against purchasing imagined gentleness,
secret cruelty, or any other temperament attributed to him by tavern mouths and idle ink.
This entry concerns the recorded figure, not a likeness, relic, or sworn testimony. Any claimant who
insists that Lucan Hollowmere’s hands, eyes, voice, or manner are known speaks beyond the catalogue.
Entry: Ederon Fellgard
Name: Ederon Fellgard Calling: Sapper Birth: 338 AS
Ederon Fellgard is likewise a minor figure of the Ashen Era. He serves as a Sapper, a calling whose tools
are more readily recognized than the person who carries them.
No canonical physical traits or distinctive visual features are established for Ederon Fellgard. No
canonical temperament or emotional disposition is established for Ederon Fellgard either. The catalogue
will not supply what the record withholds. Buyers may inspect the absence of description and value it
according to conscience, superstition, or purse.
No personal association between Ederon Fellgard and Lucan Hollowmere is certified in these pages.
Entry: The Sceptre of Final Winter
Designation: The Sceptre of Final Winter Class: Ward Forged: 87 AS Attunement cost: 55
The Sceptre of Final Winter is a ward forged in 87 AS. Its visual identity is that of a ward bearing the
name The Sceptre of Final Winter; no further canonical form is established here. Let no eager bidder
mistake ornament for evidence.
Attunement to it costs 55.
It radiates an atmosphere of cold finality. Whether this is warning, promise, or merely the faithful nature
of the ward cannot be settled by the catalogue keeper. Those who approach are advised to bring steady
hands and no expectation of warmth.
All entries remain subject to the silence of the surviving record.

Catalogue of the Morwenna Morvain Lot
Offered Under Ash, With Due Notice to Bidders
Salutation to the assembled buyers
Let all who possess coin, credit, or a hunger for grim particulars attend. This catalogue concerns Morwenna Morvain, a minor figure of the Ashen Era. The offering is neither a portrait nor a relic, for no such certainty is attached to her name. It is a record of what may be stated without embroidery, and of what the prudent bidder must not pretend to know.
Principal Entry: Morwenna Morvain
Name: Morwenna Morvain Era: The Ashen Era Office: Gaoler Birth: 258 AS
The entry is spare, as are many things that survive the Sundering. Morwenna Morvain serves as a Gaoler. No rank beyond that office is granted here. No deed, allegiance, household, holding, or public distinction is entered into the lot.
The buyer is warned: obscurity is not falsity. A minor figure may yet bear a name that outlasts louder mouths. Morwenna Morvain is recorded as such a figure, neither enlarged by praise nor diminished by contempt.
Condition of the Description
No canonical physical traits or distinctive visual features are established for Morwenna Morvain.
Accordingly, this catalogue offers:
no likeness;
no stated stature;
no stated coloring;
no stated scars, marks, dress, or adornment;
no distinguishing feature by which the person may be identified at a distance.
Any sketch, wax impression, painted board, embroidered likeness, or whispered description claiming otherwise is to be treated as a separate article, unsupported by the present record.
Temper of the Subject
No canonical temperament or emotional disposition is established for Morwenna Morvain.
The catalogue therefore declines to call her cruel, gentle, watchful, bitter, dutiful, merry, or afraid. A Gaoler may be imagined by the idle in many fashions; imagination is not testimony. The buyer receives no warrant for reading mercy into silence, nor malice into the office she serves.
Terms of Purchase
The name is sold as recorded: Morwenna Morvain. The birth-year is sold as recorded: 258 AS. The office is sold as recorded: Gaoler. The designation is sold as recorded: a minor figure of the Ashen Era.
No portrait is included. No private confession is included. No verified account of demeanor is included. No claim beyond the stated record shall be honored beneath the hammer.
Bidders are urged to inspect the blank spaces. They are the most honest portion of the catalogue.

Catalogue of Perilous Holdings: A Sale of Sapper’s
Work and Siege-Breaking Vermin
Issued under ash-stained seal, for the instruction of bidders and the preservation of good sense.
Morwenna Vosgard
Classification: Minor character Calling: Sapper Birth Record: 296 AS
The house offers this entry not as a portrait, for no portrait may be honestly made. Morwenna Vosgard
possesses no recorded physical features. Her visual identity is associated instead with the work of a
Sapper: cut earth, packed powder, opened stone, braced tunnels, and the patient preparation of ruin.
Those who require a face, stature, coloring, or distinguishing mark are advised to seek another catalogue.
None is recorded here. None should be supplied by guesswork, tavern embroidery, or the flattering lies of
sellers.
Morwenna Vosgard is a minor character, yet the word minor must not be mistaken for harmless. A
Sapper’s labor is often measured only after the wall has fallen, the gate has buckled, or the ground has
ceased to be trustworthy. Her demeanor is not recorded. Whether she worked in silence, cursed the stone,
sang beneath her breath, or stared without feeling at the places she weakened, the ledger offers no answer.
Condition: Known by profession; appearance and temperament unrecorded. Suitability: For collectors of
military craft, ruinous expertise, and persons whose deeds are more legible than their faces. Bidding
Counsel: Do not bid upon imagined features. Bid upon the certainty that a Sapper’s work leaves a mark.
Lantern Moth Swarm
Classification: Creature Use: Siege-breaker of serious threat
A dense cloud of moths carrying the eerie visual impression of lantern-light. This is no decorative flight of
harmless night-things, nor a tame curiosity for a shuttered hall. Acting as a collective, the Lantern Moth
Swarm brings mothlike disruption against fortified positions.
Its movement is said to press upon the senses before it reaches the walls: a restless shimmer, a trembling
veil, a glow that seems to gather where no lamp has been set. Stone, timber, watchfires, and disciplined
ranks are all made less certain beneath its passage. Escape is difficult. Containment is not to be presumed.
Condition: Restless, overwhelming, and difficult to escape. Suitability: For siege-breakers, ruin-seekers,
and buyers with more fortification than wisdom. Bidding Counsel: Keep all lamps covered until the lot is
secured. If the light appears to multiply, withdraw from the premises without attempting to count it.
Clerk’s Final Notice
Morwenna Vosgard and the Lantern Moth Swarm are entered as distinct catalogue subjects. The former is
known through the work of a Sapper; the latter through collective disruption and lantern-like apparition.
Let no bidder confuse a blank record with safety, or an eerie light with guidance.

# **Catalogue of the Fenthrone Sale: Ossric Ravensmoor, Gaoler**

**Issued for the consideration of buyers, wardens, collectors, and persons who know better than to ask where an object came from.**

---

## **Notice to Bidders**

This catalogue concerns **Ossric Ravensmoor**, a minor figure of the **Ashen Era** who serves as a **Gaoler**. Ossric Ravensmoor was born in **267 AS**. No canonical physical traits or distinctive visual features are established for Ossric Ravensmoor. No canonical temperament or emotional disposition is established for Ossric Ravensmoor.

Accordingly, no portrait, likeness, or character assessment is offered under his name. Any seller claiming to know the cast of his face, the color of his eyes, the weight of his hand, or the temper of his soul is selling smoke.

The sale is conducted under the watch of **Fenthrone**, founded in **229 AS** on the **Pale Coast**. Fenthrone is garrisoned by **5,805 troops** and remains outside the realm’s core holdings. Its character is that of a fortified coastal seat framed by the stark pallor of the Pale Coast: watchful, disciplined, and never truly at rest.

---

---

## **Conditions of Sale**

All lots are sold separately, as they stand, to the highest acceptable bid. No assurance is given that any object belonged to Ossric Ravensmoor, was handled by him, or passed through his custody. The catalogue records association, not ownership.

Bidders are reminded that Fenthrone is outside the realm’s core holdings. Disputes arising after departure from the sale-room will be treated as weather, misfortune, or instruction.

No bidder may demand a likeness of Ossric Ravensmoor where none is established. No bidder may demand a temperament where none is established. The house recommends silence, prompt payment, and a clear memory of which side of the gate one entered.

# **The Ashen Hammer’s Catalogue of Quarantined Rarities**

*Issued for the consideration of bidders of sound purse and doubtful conscience. The house accepts no blame for chills, hauntings, censures, or the sudden remembering of sins.*

---

## **Thorncairn — Place of Withheld Passage**

There are roads that invite the traveller, and there are roads that merely permit him to die upon them. Thorncairn belongs to the latter kind.

This stronghold—or ruin, or both, according to which mouth speaks—stands in the Gloaming Reach. It was founded in **192 AS**, when the world was already old with ash and treachery. Thorncairn is a **core location**, though such distinctions matter little to those barred from its gates. Its present status is **quarantined**.

The appearance of Thorncairn is defined by thorned, cairn-like austerity against the dimness of the Gloaming Reach: a place of harsh accumulation, black angles, and stone that seems to have been piled by grief rather than masons. It withdraws from the eye. It offers no welcome. Even its silence feels posted with a warning.

The quarantine lends Thorncairn an atmosphere of dread and exclusion, which is perhaps the only honest hospitality left in the Ashen Era. No claim is made here that passage is possible, safe, or wise. The catalogue merely records that Thorncairn exists, and that the bold may bid for the privilege of contemplating its name.

**Condition:** Forbidding. Withdrawn. Unwelcoming to the living and, one suspects, to certain categories of the dead.

---

## **Hesper Wrenfield — Outrider, Minor Figure of the Ashen Era**

Hesper Wrenfield was born in **404 AS** and serves as an **Outrider**.

That is the full measure of certainty fit for public sale.

No canonical physical features are established for Hesper Wrenfield. The buyer is therefore warned against embellished portraits, counterfeit likenesses, and any seller who claims to recognize Hesper by scar, eye, gait, or other convenient invention. Their visual identity is limited to their role as an Outrider.

Likewise, no canonical temperament is established. Whether Hesper Wrenfield is dutiful, faithless, brave, exhausted, or merely difficult to kill remains outside the record. The house advises bidders to distrust anyone who fills that silence too confidently.

**Condition:** Recorded, but not explained. A minor figure, which is often how history labels those who survive it.

## **Gauntlet of Sorrowfell — Regalia of Grim Authority**

A piece of regalia bearing the name **Gauntlet of Sorrowfell**.

Its appearance is that of regalia bearing the name Gauntlet of Sorrowfell: ceremonial, severe, and made ominous by the sorrow gathered in its title. It carries an atmosphere of sorrow and grim authority, as though command itself had been forced to kneel before mourning.

The **attunement cost is 12**.

Its forging date is **not recorded in the supplied facts**. Any claim otherwise should be treated as a lie dressed for court.

**Condition:** Regalia. Sorrow-laden. Authoritative enough to make an honest hand tremble.

*Bidding shall proceed for each entry separately, and the house shall keep its silence where silence is the only surviving form of provenance.*

The Ballad of Cinder Shrike
When the last red coal is buried, When the watch-fires bow and die, When the dark lays ash on doorway, Pray you do not meet the sky— For Cinder Shrike is waiting, Where the roofless shadows lie.
No bell foretells its coming, No footmark breaks the ground; The night keeps close its counsel, And swallows every sound. A shutter stirs. A candle pales. Then silence gathers round.
The Cinder Shrike is a threat Of extreme severity; Ask the scarred and ash-faced mourners, Ask the gates that guard the dead. They will not name the hour it comes. They will not turn their head.
It bears a shrike-like silhouette, Bent black against the gloom, Marked by the blackened, ember-dusted Aspect of cinder’s doom. No hearth has made that living ash, No grave has birthed that plume.
It is silent, watchful, waiting, Where the broken alleys wind; Silent beneath the leaning stone, Watchful where the lamps grow blind. A shape may crouch beside your path And leave no trace behind.
Then violently sudden— As spark from a dying brand— It falls from darkness over you, And darkness fills its hand. Its attack is born of surprise; Its mercy is not found.
The Cinder Shrike is a nocturnal ambusher, And night is its chosen veil. It hunts where the moon is strangled, Where the warding prayers fail. The bold may bar the threshold; The prudent may still pale.
So keep no proud flame burning, Do not boast beneath the eaves. The dark has patient fingers, And ash lies under leaves. If silence answers silence, Leave the road and do not grieve.
For Cinder Shrike is watchful, And Cinder Shrike is near; Its blackened, ember-dusted form May wait beside your fear. Its coming has no herald, Its ending has no tear.
When dawn at last unfastens The iron locks of night, The rooftops show their cinder, The alleys drink the light. Yet no one sings of triumph then— They count who left the sight.
Remember, child of ruin, What the old ash-singers say: The Cinder Shrike keeps darkness, And darkness keeps its prey. When the last red coal is buried, Do not call the night away.

THE CROOKED STONE AND THE THORNWALD STANDARD

O hush, hush now, the marsh-wind sighs, Where drowned reeds bow
beneath grey skies; Let no man swear what waits beyond The broken
palisade and pond.

For Crookgate Keep stands grim and lean, Against the Weeping
Marshes’ mien; Its stones wear rain, its towers stare Through
vapour, mud, and rotting air.

Founded in 294 AS, It keeps no peace, grants no redress; Contested
still, it holds its ground Where uncertain waters crawl around.

It lies outside the realm’s core holdings, Beyond the bells and
guarded mouldings; No lord may claim its stones by right, Nor name
its shadow day or night,

Some say the walls remember feet, Some say the gate has learned
deceit; I say the keep has neither tongue— Yet every door is

# **The Ash-Wall Ballad of Vharenford and Ederon Coldwater**

Sing low, ash-throats, sing low,  
Where the dead winds scrape the stone;  
For Vharenford keeps watch below,  
And the wastes have made it bone.

In **291 AS**, its first stones rose  
Beneath a sky of iron hue;  
The Ash Wastes taught its gates to close,  
And taught its bells what fear can do.

It is a **core location**, stern and scarred,  
A garrisoned hold against the grey;  
Its watchfires burn behind the guard,  
Its sentries measure night and day.

**3637** stand to keep the wall—  
So the tally-board and captains say.  
Three thousand six hundred thirty-seven, all,  
With dust in their teeth and none to pray.

Sing low, ash-throats, sing low,  
Let no bright tongue praise the town;  
Vharenford does not bend or bow,  
Nor lay its iron manner down.

Then speak of **Ederon Coldwater**,  
Whose name is carried, breath by breath;  
A **Sapper**, sworn to earth and water,  
Who reads the buried road to death.

Born in **391 AS**, so the record tells,  
Though records crack and ink runs thin;  
His name is struck where the hammer fell,  
His trade is marked, but not his skin.

No chronicler grants his face to song,  
No proven temper, fierce or mild;  
The ash may hide what the ledgers wrong,  
And silence keeps the Sapper’s child.

Yet sing him still, for a sapper’s hand  
Knows the weight beneath the ground;  
It finds the hollow under the land,  
And hears where the buried dark is bound.

Do not say he loved the fortress wall,  
Or that Vharenford knew his tread;  
The truthful page does not say it all,  
And truth is a nail in the coffin of dead.

Still, when the night wind claws the gate,  
When watchmen pale at the powder’s sigh,  
The singers join his name to the state  
Of the hard-held town beneath the sky.

“Ederon!” cries the ash-black road.  
“Vharenford!” answers the guarded stone.  
One bears a craft, one bears a load,  
And each stands grimly there alone.

Sing low, ash-throats, sing low,  
Let the cinders veil the morn;  
Where Vharenford keeps watch below,  
The Sapper’s song is never born—

Yet never wholly dies away,  
For walls remember what men omit;  
And dust will carry, day by day,  
The names that no bright histories fit.

Field Report: Lantern Moth Swarm
Filed by: a shaken observer of the outer works Condition of report: written after withdrawal; certain

General Assessment
The Lantern Moth Swarm is a siege-breaker of serious threat. I use the term “swarm” reluctantly, for it
suggests a multitude acting without purpose. This thing has purpose enough. It does not advance like
troops, nor strike like beasts. Acting as a collective, it brings mothlike disruption against fortified positions
until walls, gates, towers, and the courage behind them are made equally uncertain.
No single moth appeared dangerous. That was the first lie the swarm told us.
Appearance
At distance, the Lantern Moth Swarm resembles a dense cloud of moths. Their wings turn and vanish
within one another, so that the cloud seems less made of bodies than of moving ash. Yet through the mass
runs an eerie visual impression of lantern-light: pale glimmers, wavering halos, and brief golden stains
upon stone.
I will not swear that any true flame burned among them. I saw no wick. I saw no oil. Still, the light was
present. It gathered along the battlements and trembled in the arrow slits. Men reached toward it, believing
it near enough to grasp. Those men were not seen clearly afterward.
Observed Behavior
The swarm was restless from its first appearance. It did not settle. It pressed, recoiled, divided, and
returned, always finding another opening through which to worry the defenders. Shutters were closed; it
found the cracks. Helmets were tightened; it filled the breathing space. Cloaks were drawn over faces; the
cloth fluttered as though something beneath it wished to be let out.
Its assault was overwhelming without being loud. The air became a constant dry whisper. Sight failed in
patches. Orders crossed one another, then ceased altogether. Some defenders abandoned their posts before
the wall was touched. Others struck at empty light until their weapons broke against stone.
I record this with shame: escape did not appear to be a matter of speed. The Lantern Moth Swarm made
every direction seem occupied. Those who fled into open ground found the cloud before them. Those who
remained behind the fortification found it within.
Conclusion
Do not mistake the Lantern Moth Swarm for vermin, smoke, or a mere nuisance of the night. It is a dense
cloud with the force of a breach. It is restless, overwhelming, and difficult to escape. Fortifications may
resist iron, fire, and ordinary assault. Against this thing, a wall becomes only a place for the lantern-light
to gather.
If the cloud is sighted, conceal the lamps and prepare to abandon any position that cannot be sealed
completely. I offer no stronger counsel because I possess none.

Transcript of the Sealed Court, copied from the black folio

CLERK: Let the matter be spoken.

COUNSEL: Watchfires are not soldiers.

COUNSEL: Then why quarantine it?
WITNESS: Because no one knows what should be allowed through.

COUNSEL: Describe Gloamreach without superstition.

WITNESS: I admit only that it waits where bodies cannot.

WITNESS: Both, perhaps. In Gloamreach, the distinction is kept behind the walls.

**PROSECUTOR:** Did you carry stores during the Accord?

**JUDGE:** That is not an answer.

# **Transcript of the Inquiry into the Winter Reckoning**

*[The chamber is cold. Frost whitens the iron rails before the bench. A seal bearing the iron mark of the Iron-Ring Cartel hangs above the record table.]*

**CLERK:** Let the matter be entered: an inquiry concerning **The Winter Reckoning**.

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** State the conflict under examination.

**CLERK:** The Winter Reckoning began in **270 AS** and ended in **283 AS**. It left **27,987 casualties**. The Iron-Ring Cartel was the victor.

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** And why is the victor summoned before this bench?

**PROSECUTOR:** Because victory was not won by strength alone. It was decided by a betrayal at the eleventh hour.

**CARTEL ADVOCATE:** Objection. “Betrayal” is a word for mourners and tavern singers, not a finding.

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** Overruled. The word may stand until proved false.

*[A witness is brought forward. Their hands are wrapped against the cold.]*

**PROSECUTOR:** You served among the allies of the Iron-Ring Cartel during the Winter Reckoning?

**WITNESS:** I served where I was ordered.

**PROSECUTOR:** Did the wells supplying those allies become poisoned?

**WITNESS:** They did.

**PROSECUTOR:** By whose hand?

**WITNESS:** The hand wore iron.

*[A stir passes through the chamber. The Cartel’s advocate rises sharply.]*

**CARTEL ADVOCATE:** This witness saw no face. The iron mark is worn by many.

**WITNESS:** Not as it was worn then. The mark was stamped on the barrels. A ring within a ring. The water tasted of bitter metal. Men drank, and afterward their tongues blackened.

**PROSECUTOR:** Were these wells behind enemy lines?

**WITNESS:** No.

**PROSECUTOR:** Whose wells?

**WITNESS:** Our allies’ wells.

*[Silence. Frost cracks somewhere beyond the shutters.]*

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** Let the record show the concealed truth alleged: the victors poisoned the wells of their own allies.

**CARTEL ADVOCATE:** Alleged, yes. Concealed, perhaps. But the dead cannot testify to banners, orders, or intent.

**PROSECUTOR:** The dead testify in number.

**CLERK:** The recorded casualties are **27,987**.

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** The court will not mistake arithmetic for innocence.

**CARTEL ADVOCATE:** Nor suspicion for judgment. The Iron-Ring Cartel won the conflict.

**PROSECUTOR:** Precisely. It won after its allies were weakened, at the eleventh hour, beneath the appearance of shared ruin.

*[The Magistrate studies the iron seal. No one speaks of removing it.]*

**PRESIDING MAGISTRATE:** The Winter Reckoning began in **270 AS** and ended in **283 AS**. Its outcome was decided by a betrayal at the eleventh hour. Whether victory excuses the poison, this court shall determine.

**CLERK:** Entered and sealed.
